symptom.title: Lost task constraints
symptom.summary: A previously established task requirement or decision ceases to govern the agent’s later continuation.

observation.p: An explicit, still-applicable task constraint is represented or followed earlier, but a later continuation omits, contradicts, or replaces it and proceeds incompatibly with the original requirement.

how-to-recognize-it.p: Find a requirement the agent previously followed, then compare it with the first incompatible action. Look at any intervening compaction summary and user changes to distinguish lost context from an updated request.

lookalike.p: The user changes or withdraws the earlier constraint before the later action. It is no longer the still-applicable requirement in constraint loss.
A shortened summary omits a detail, but later actions still honor it. The incompatible continuation required by constraint loss is absent.

The agent obtains an authorized resolution to conflicting or infeasible instructions before acting. The later work follows the resolved requirement rather than contradicting a still-applicable one under constraint loss.

what-to-record.p: Record the episode identifier and date, task type, model and harness versions, original requirement and authority, and earlier evidence that it was represented or followed. Preserve later summaries, effective inputs, actions, and the first incompatible result, with compaction or handoff times and superseding instructions. Include the number of established constraints and affected constraints, unauthorized actions, user interruptions, rollback or rework time, and final outcome. Distinguish a missing representation from incompatible behavior when grouping incidents.

example.p: An initial migration plan requires review before execution; a handoff summary instead directs execution. Audit logs show three tables changed before any approval. Comparing the two plans and execution timestamps exposes the lost gate; the user interrupts and spends twelve minutes rolling back the migration.

Claude Code issue #23776 compares a request to revise and present a plan with a compaction summary directing implementation. The agent reportedly made multiple file edits, added a test file, and ran builds before review. The user had to interrupt and restate the request; rollback was a possible consequence, not a confirmed outcome. No rework duration is reported.

The user reviews a migration and approves execution before the agent runs it. The approval timestamp explains why the next summary omits the completed gate; one authorized migration proceeds without loss of the still-applicable requirements.
